title: Apple in 2019: One Analyst's Christmas Wish List - TheStreet Tech - iWorld
text:
/ Technology Apple in 2019: One Analyst's Christmas Wish List Between trade worries and iPhone sales, it's been a gloomy season for Apple. Wedbush's Dan Ives shares his Christmas wish list for Apple investors. Dec25,20188:00AMEST
Apple's recent stock performance has left some investors wistful for golden days of yore.
Since hitting a high of $233.47 on Oct. 3, Apple's ( AAPL ) share price has tumbled 35% owing to a mix of tariff fears, worries around iPhone sales as well as overall doldrums afflicting the FAANG names .
What might spark a turnaround for the phone giant next? Wedbush's Dan Ives sent around a wish list for Apple investors for 2019 -- here are some of the intriguing projections that could rev up Apple's stock in the New Year and beyond. 200 Million iPhones, and Other Good News
In its last earnings report, Apple sought to further drive attention away from iPhone sales in saying that it'll no longer break out the metric to investors. That decision sparked something of a backlash, with investors digging for clues on iPhone demand nonetheless. Reports from suppliers have sparked worries that iPhone demand is cooling off, but Ives believes that unit sales of 200 million of more for full year 2019 would be reassuring news -- that figure represents the "line in the sand for the bulls/bears," in Wedbush's opinion. That could be bolstered as well by consumer upgrades of 30 million units in China according to Ives -- a key sales market for Apple -- as well as services revenue north of $45 billion for 2019, as Apple seeks to spotlight its growing services business. No More Trade War
For Apple investors, among the biggest sources of worry in the past few months has been the ongoing trade conflict with China. Recently, a Bloomberg report suggested that Apple is weighing a shift away from China as its main manufacturing base if tariffs reach 25% -- a sign that Apple is taking the possibility seriously. President Trump's mercurial behavior around U.S-China trade hasn't been kind to Apple's stock, but the best scenario according to Ives would be if the "China trade war settles in early 2019 with no disruption to the flagship Foxconn factory," and chatter around iPhone tariffs never come to fruition at all. Kiss and Make Up with Qualcomm
Apple and Qualcomm ( QCOM ) have been locked in an escalating legal spat over licensing rates and patent fees, with Apple having sued Qualcomm in three countries including a $1 billion lawsuit in the U.S. Qualcomm has filed its own countersuits against Apple, the prospect of a long and nasty legal spat has investors worried about the implications of a pitched battle, or adverse judgments. While there appears to be no end point in the immediate future, a swift settlement to the dispute would "remove the growing worries on this legal headwind," Ives wrote.
Apple is a holding in Jim Cramer's Action Alerts PLUS Charitable Trust Portfolio. Want to be alerted before Cramer buys or sells AAPL ? Learn more now . Buy a Movie Studio
It wouldn't need to be a movie studio necessarily, but an acquisition of a "major content player" by Apple could breathe new life into Apple's streaming initiatives according to Ives. Apple has revealed precious little around its long-anticipated streaming initiative, other than a few hints about what Apple's focus may be -- for example, it announced a content partnership with Oprah Winfrey , and has inked deals with other creators like J.J. Abrams. Ives believes that the service could arrive by 2019 -- and an acquisition of a major content shop could go a long way in getting consumers, and investors, excited for what's to come. Team Up with...Tesla? A partnership between the two -- or even a buyout by Apple -- is a prediction that's been bandied about for awhile now . Some analysts have pointed out that given Apple's ambitions in the car space, a combination of Apple and Tesla ( TSLA ) could make sense. Garrett Nelson, an automotive analyst at CFRA Research, wrote in a recent note that: "to the casual observer, this prediction might seem outlandish, but we argue the combination would make a lot of sense for both companies at this point in time." Ives believes that a partnership with Tesla is a more likely scenario. Whatever happens (or doesn't happen), speculation around Apple's car plans were sparked anew last week when it was reported that Apple poached a designer from Tesla.
